$comment: Ping layer spec. The canvas is the master's own pixel size; nothing is resampled. Regions ([x, y, w, h], the box a layer's visible pixels may occupy) and pivots ([x, y], the point a layer rotates and scales around) are not typed in: scripts/regions.mjs measures them on the master with the rules below and writes art/regions.json, which is frozen once the author approves the master. Every layer is a full-canvas transparent PNG in art/layers/<id>.png. Draw order is z, low to high.
canvas: the master's pixel size, measured into art/regions.json

regionRule.$comment: Chosen before any master existed. All lengths in pixels, rounded up. Blobs come from the master compared with 02-head.png (the empty screen) after aligning it: pixels whose largest channel differs by more than processing.featureLo, joined when closer than the margin (dilated by ceil(margin / 2)), blobs under margin x margin pixels ignored.
regionRule.screen: the master's head silhouette bounding box (outline plus its bright halo); screenWidth is its width; margin = ceil(screenWidth * 3 / 100)
regionRule.head: screen box grown by the margin, clamped to the canvas
regionRule.changedAfterSeeing: The interior, cursor and head-pixel rules below were changed after seeing G1-01 and G2-01 (author's prompt #8): the first rule also searched the outline, where a redrawn empty screen differs in thin rims, and took the cursor as a red blob, which joined it with a recoloured chevron.
regionRule.interior: changed after seeing G1-01 and G2-01: face features are searched only inside the screen (the largest dark area inside the silhouette with everything it encloses), shrunk inward by the margin. Differences on the outline are drift, not regions. Pixels lit in the empty screen (max channel >= processing.silhouetteThreshold: the chevron, the outline) belong to the head, never to a feature; feature extraction skips them too.
regionRule.cursor: changed after seeing G1-01 and G2-01: the master's red pixels inside the screen (R minus the larger of G and B above processing.featureLo); their box grown by the margin. The chevron is part of the head.
regionRule.eyes: the blobs except the lowest one; exactly two expected; their joint box grown by the margin
regionRule.mouth: the lowest blob, box w x h. Every mouth shape keeps the closed smile's top edge and opens downward, so the region runs from the box top minus the margin down to the box top plus max(h, ceil(2w / 3)) plus the margin (room for 'open' and 'round', 4 blocks tall under a 6-block smile), and is centred on the box horizontally with half-width ceil(3w / 4) + margin (room for 'wide', 1.5 times as wide)
regionRule.brows: the eyes region's x range; from the eyes region's top up by ceil(eyesHeight / 2) + margin
regionRule.overlaps: eyes and mouth regions are split at the middle of the gap between the measured eyes and mouth boxes; the brows region's top is cut to the cursor region's bottom if they overlap; any overlap left after that rejects the master
regionRule.clamp: every feature region is clamped to the head region

pivotRule.head: bottom centre of the screen box
pivotRule.cursor: centre of the measured cursor box
pivotRule.eyes: centre of the measured eyes box
pivotRule.mouth: centre of the measured mouth box

layers.about: the soft neon halo around the screen, everything outside the head silhouette, alpha from brightness
the screen with no eyes, brows, mouth or cursor; keeps the logo's prompt chevron
the logo's red cursor block, its own layer so it can blink
both eyes, open, the logo's shapes
both eyes closed: a bar along each eye's bottom edge; swapped with eyes_open for blinks
both brows, neutral; not in the logo or the master, their own edit so the layer can be dropped without regenerating anything

layers.covers: silence, M, B, P (lips closed); also F, V
layers.about: closed mouth, the logo's pixel smile: the default between words and the shape every M/B/P closure must hit, or speech looks mumbled

layers.covers: most consonants (T D N S Z K G L R H TH CH J) and unstressed vowels (schwa, IH, EH)
layers.about: slightly open: the most frequent speaking shape; without it the mouth snaps between closed and wide

layers.covers: open stressed vowels AA, AE, AH, AY, AW
layers.about: wide open: loud open vowels and stressed syllables, the peak of each word

layers.covers: rounded vowels and glides O, OO, OW, OY, UW, W, also SH and ER
layers.about: small ring: the one shape that is about lip rounding, not openness; 'you', 'go', 'what' read wrong without it

layers.covers: spread vowels E, I, EE, EY, IY
layers.about: wide and flat: the spread-lips opposite of mouth_round; also usable as a grin

dropped.reason: F/V is read from the upper teeth resting on the lower lip. Ping's mouth is a flat shape of neon pixel blocks with no teeth and no lips, so an F/V shape would look the same as mouth_rest or mouth_small; F and V map to mouth_rest.

processing.$comment: Chosen parameters, not measurements. Values are 0..255 channel levels unless named Px.

checks.$comment: Canvas size, inside-region and corner alpha are pass/fail from the start. Inside-region has two parts: the layer's alpha box inside its region, and (added after the first real run showed that feature layers are cut to their region, so their box alone could never fail) every blob a variant changed against the master inside the screen lies inside the regions of the layers it is meant to change (lib/pipeline.mjs changedBlobs). Offset, drift and screen scale are only measured until limits are chosen after looking at the first real run; null means not set yet. drift = mean absolute RGB difference from the master outside the changed feature, after alignment, 0..255 scale. scale = the variant's screen box size minus the master's.
